tatiana-by-kwame-onwuachi-new-york.our_story: Chef Kwame Onwuachi opened Tatiana at Lincoln Center to tell a New York story rooted in Nigeria, Jamaica, and the Bronx—fine dining that feels personal, bold, and unmistakably diaspora.
tatiana-by-kwame-onwuachi-new-york.cultural_roots: Afro-Caribbean and Nigerian flavors reframed for Lincoln Center: heritage techniques, luxury ingredients, and the rhythm of New York nightlife on one plate.

d-gon-washington.our_story: Dōgon at The Wharf brings Afro-Caribbean fine dining to the Potomac waterfront—an elegant room where Chesapeake ingredients meet West Indian spice and technique.
d-gon-washington.cultural_roots: Named for the historic Dogon heritage, the menu honors African and Caribbean culinary lineages while celebrating Washington's role as a global diaspora capital.

atx-fine-001.our_story: Chef Kevin Falcón's Canje takes its name from Guyana's national bird, serving a love letter to the Caribbean—from pepperpot to suya—in a lush East Austin dining room.
atx-fine-001.cultural_roots: A pan-Caribbean lens on Guyana, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico: wood fire, tropical produce, and the spice traditions that traveled with island communities to Texas.

chopnblok-downtown-houston.our_story: ChòpnBlọk reimagines West African fast-fine at POST Houston—Chef Kehinde Ogunsanya's bowls, grills, and cocktails built for diners who want jollof and suya with design-forward hospitality.
chopnblok-downtown-houston.cultural_roots: Nigerian and Ghanaian street-to-table culture: communal bowls, bold pepper, and the chop-bar spirit of Lagos and Accra translated for modern Houston.

demera-ethiopian-chicago.our_story: Chef Tigist Reda built Demera into Chicago's benchmark for Ethiopian dining—injera, honey wine, and shared platters served with the warmth of a family gathering in Uptown.
demera-ethiopian-chicago.cultural_roots: Habesha hospitality: eating from one platter signifies trust and friendship; berbere, tej, and slow-stewed wats carry centuries of Ethiopian table culture.

mia-red-rooster-overtown.our_story: Marcus Samuelsson's Red Rooster Overtown anchors Historic Overtown with art, music, and plates that honor Black American and Caribbean culinary history—from yardbird to coconut-smoked oxtails.
mia-red-rooster-overtown.cultural_roots: Overtown's legacy as a Black cultural capital meets Afro-Caribbean and Southern traditions: soul, jazz, and the Shrine nights that keep the neighborhood's spirit alive.

sa-jerk-shack.our_story: Chef Nicola Blaque brought The Jerk Shack to San Antonio to prove Jamaican cooking belongs in the fine-dining conversation—smoke, spice, and patty-shop soul with Michelin recognition.
sa-jerk-shack.cultural_roots: Jerk pit culture from Jamaica: pimento, scotch bonnet, and slow smoke over pimento wood—the flavors that define island cookouts and corner shops alike.

nola-dakar.our_story: Chef Serigne Mbaye's Dakar NOLA traces a tasting menu from Senegal to Louisiana—one seating, one narrative, showing how West African food shaped Creole cuisine.
nola-dakar.cultural_roots: The Senegalese thieboudienne lineage runs through New Orleans gumbo pots: rice, fish, okra, and spice carried across the Atlantic and reborn on Magazine Street.

phi-fine-001.our_story: Friday Saturday Sunday turns a Rittenhouse rowhouse into an eight-course journey where chefs Jonah and Chad Williams weave West African and Caribbean seasoning into modern American tasting menus.
phi-fine-001.cultural_roots: Philadelphia's rowhouse intimacy meets diaspora spice memory—technique from fine dining, flavor from the African and Caribbean communities that season the city's kitchens.

kann-portland.our_story: Chef Gregory Gourdet's Kann is a wood-fired Haitian restaurant that put Portland on the global map—open kitchen, cane sugar glaze, and the pride of a James Beard-winning room.
kann-portland.cultural_roots: Haitian cuisine at the hearth: wood fire, epis, and island produce; Kann honors Ayiti's culinary independence with every flame-kissed plate.

chs-fine-001.our_story: Chef Bintou N'Daw opened Bintü Atelier in Charleston to elevate West African staples—heritage jollof, egusi, and fufu—with the precision of the city's fine-dining scene.
chs-fine-001.cultural_roots: Senegalese and broader West African techniques meet Lowcountry hospitality: rice, stew, and spice traditions presented with minimalist, chef-driven elegance.

communion-r-b-seattle.our_story: Kristian Bowers and Chef Kristi Brown's Communion R&B redefined Seattle soul food—Hood Sushi, catfish, and a Central District room where Black creativity meets the plate.
communion-r-b-seattle.cultural_roots: Seattle's Central District soul lineage: Southern comfort, Japanese technique, and the fusion spirit of a neighborhood that fed the city's Black arts renaissance.

atx-fine-002.our_story: Ember Kitchen is Austin live-fire theater—a Josper oven overlooking Lady Bird Lake, where Latin-Caribbean flavors meet smoke, prawns, and plantain in a moody Seaholm dining room.
atx-fine-002.cultural_roots: Caribbean and Latin American fire cooking: charcoal, citrus, and spice at the intersection of Gulf Coast heat and Austin's cosmopolitan dining culture.

atl-fine-001.our_story: Lucian Books and Wine pairs a curated bookstore with Buckhead fine dining—modern Afro-European plates, heritage pork, and a wine program as intellectual as the shelves.
atl-fine-001.cultural_roots: A salon for Atlanta's diaspora: African ingredient stories told beside European technique, with wine and literature framing every meal as conversation.

lucia-los-angeles.our_story: Lucia brings Afro-Caribbean fine dining to Fairfax—jerk lobster, craft cocktails, and late-night energy that treats island flavor as luxury, not afterthought.
lucia-los-angeles.cultural_roots: Caribbean spice and LA nightlife culture: jerk, rum, and seafood traditions remixed for a city that celebrates bold flavor and late tables.

hou-reggae-hut.our_story: Reggae Hut Cafe has been a Third Ward institution for decades—brown stew fish, jerk chicken, and patties served with the easy warmth of a neighborhood Caribbean kitchen.
hou-reggae-hut.cultural_roots: Houston's Caribbean community on Almeda: Jamaican patty shops, stew pots, and reggae spirit—the everyday dining room where island families gather after church and work.
